transcript.en: Hello everyone. Today we're going to look at another natural food product and that's maple syrup.
transcript.zh: 大家好。今天我们来了解一种天然食品，那就是枫糖浆。

transcript.en: What is this exactly? Well, maple syrup looks rather like clear honey, but it's not made by bees; it's produced from the plant fluid
transcript.zh: 枫糖浆到底是什么呢？它看起来很像纯蜂蜜 但却不是由蜜蜂产生的；它是由枫树内部的植物液体

transcript.en: - or sap - inside the maple tree and that makes maple syrup a very natural product.
transcript.zh: 也就是树液产生的，这使得枫糖浆成为一种纯天然的产品。

transcript.en: Maple syrup is a thick, golden, sweet-tasting liquid that can be bought in bottles or jars and poured onto food such as waffles and ice cream or used in the baking of cakes and pastries.
transcript.zh: 枫糖浆是一种粘稠的、金黄色的 甜味的液体，可以装在瓶子或罐子里购买，可以倒在华夫饼 冰淇淋等食物上，也可以用来烘烤蛋糕和糕点。

transcript.en: It contains no preservatives or added ingredients, and it provides a healthy alternative to refined sugar.
transcript.zh: 它不含任何防腐剂或添加成分可以用作精制糖的健康替代品。

transcript.en: Let's just talk a bit about the maple tree itself, which is where maple syrup comes from.
transcript.zh: 让我们来聊聊枫树本身，也就是枫糖浆的原料来源。

transcript.en: So, there are many species of maple tree, and they'll grow without fertilizer in areas where there's plenty of moisture in the soil.
transcript.zh: 枫树有很多品种，它们在土壤水分充足的地区无需施肥也能生长。

transcript.en: However, they'll only do this if another important criterion is fulfilled, which is that they must have full or partial sun exposure during the day and very cool nights - and I'll talk more about that in a minute.
transcript.zh: 不过，它们要能茁壮成长，还必须满足另一个重要条件，那就是每天需要充足的阳光或部分遮阴，并且夜晚必须非常凉爽——稍后我会详细解释这一点。

transcript.en: There are only certain parts of the world that provide all these conditions.
transcript.zh: 世界上只有某些地区可以满足以上的所有条件。

transcript.en: one is Canada, and by that, I mean all parts of Canada, and the other is the north-eastern states of North America.
transcript.zh: 一个是加拿大，我指的是加拿大的所有地区，另一个是北美的东北部各州。

transcript.en: In these areas, the climate suits the trees perfectly . In fact, Canada produces over two-thirds of the world's maple syrup
transcript.zh: 在这些地区，气候非常适合树木。事实上，加拿大生产的枫糖浆占世界总产量的三分之二以上

transcript.en: which is why the five-pointed maple leaf is a Canadian symbol and has featured on the flag since 1964.
transcript.zh: 这就是为什么五角枫叶是加拿大的象征 并且自1964年以来就成为国旗上的标志。

transcript.en: So how did maple syrup production begin? Well, long before Europeans settled in these parts of the world, the indigenous communities had started producing maple sugar.
transcript.zh: 那么，枫糖是如何开始生产的呢？嗯，早在欧洲人定居在这些地区之前 土著群体就已经开始生产枫糖了。

transcript.en: They bored holes in the trunks of maple trees and used containers made of tree bark to collect the liquid sap as it poured out.
transcript.zh: 他们在枫树树干上钻孔 用树皮制成的容器来收集流出的汁液

transcript.en: As they were unable to keep the liquid for any length of time - they didn't have storage facilities in those days
transcript.zh: 由于他们无法将这种液体保存 当时他们没有储存设施

transcript.en: - they boiled the liquid by placing pieces of rock that had become scorching hot from the sun into the sap.
transcript.zh: 所以他们将被太阳晒得灼热的岩石块放入树液中煮沸液体。

transcript.en: They did this until it turned into sugar, and they were then able to use this to sweeten their food and drinks.
transcript.zh: 直到树液变成糖 然后他们就可以用它来增加食物和饮料的甜味。

transcript.en: Since that time, improvements have been made to the process, but it has changed very little overall.
transcript.zh: 从那以后，这一生产过程有所改进 但总体上变化不大。

transcript.en: So let's look at the production of maple syrup today.
transcript.zh: 我们接下来来了解一下如今的枫糖浆的制作。

transcript.en: Clearly, the maple forests are a valuable resource in many Canadian and North American communities.
transcript.zh: 显然，枫林是加拿大和许多北美地区的宝贵资源。

transcript.en: The trees have to be well looked after and they cannot be used to make syrup until the trunks reach a diameter of around 25 centimetres.
transcript.zh: 这些树必须得到很好的照顾 它们是不能用来制造糖浆的。并且在树干直径达到25厘米左右之前。

transcript.en: This can take anything up to 40 years.
transcript.zh: 这可能需要长达40年的时间。

transcript.en: As I've already mentioned, maple trees need the right conditions to grow and also to produce sap.
transcript.zh: 正如我已经提到的 枫树需要合适的条件来生长以及分泌汁液。

transcript.en: Why is this? Well, what happens is that during a cold night, the tree absorbs water from the soil, and that rises through the tree's vascular system.
transcript.zh: 这是为什么呢？主要是由于在寒冷的夜晚 树木从土壤中吸收水分，并通过树木的脉管系统上升

transcript.en: But then in the warmer daytime, the change in temperature causes the water to be pushed back down to the bottom of the tree.
transcript.zh: 但是在温暖的白天 温度的变化导致水被推回到树的底部。

transcript.en: This continual movement - up and down - leads to the formation of the sap needed for maple syrup production.
transcript.zh: 这种不断的循环 上下移动——导致生产枫糖浆所必需的树液的形成。

transcript.en: When the tree is ready, it can be tapped and this involves drilling a small hole into the trunk and inserting a tube into it that ends in a bucket.
transcript.zh: 当树木一切条件准备好了之后，可以对其进行敲打 这个过程指的是在树干上钻一个小洞，并在里面插入一根管子，管子的末端是一个桶。

transcript.en: The trees can often take several taps, though the workers take care not to cause any damage to the healthy growth of the tree itself.
transcript.zh: 树木一般可以承受多次敲击 但工人们要小心，不要对树木本身的健康生长造成任何损害。

transcript.en: The sap that comes out of the trees consists of 98 percent water and 2 percent sugar and other nutrients.
transcript.zh: 从树中流出的汁液由98%的水 和2%的糖及其他营养成分组成。

transcript.en: It has to be boiled so that much of that water evaporates, and this process has to take place immediately, using what are called evaporators.
transcript.zh: 必须要将汁液煮沸，以便让其中大部分的水分蒸发 这个过程必须使用所谓的蒸发器立即进行处理。

transcript.en: These are basically extremely large pans - the sap is poured into these, a fire is built and the pans are then heated until the sap boils.
transcript.zh: 蒸发器其实就是非常大的锅 汁液被倒入其中 生火，然后锅被加热直到汁液沸腾。

transcript.en: As it does this, the water evaporates, and the syrup begins to form.
transcript.zh: 在这个过程中，水分蒸发 糖浆开始形成。

transcript.en: The evaporation process creates large quantities of steam, and the sap becomes thicker and denser,
transcript.zh: 蒸发过程会产生大量的蒸汽 树液变得越来越稠

transcript.en: and, at just the right moment, when the sap is thick enough to be called maple syrup, the worker removes it from the heat.
transcript.zh: 在恰当的时候，当树液稠到可以被称为枫糖浆时 工人将它从高温下移走。

transcript.en: After this process, something called 'sugar sand' has to be filtered out as this builds up during the boiling and gives the syrup a cloudy appearance and a slightly gritty taste.
transcript.zh: 经过这一过程后 一种叫做“糖沙”的东西必须被过滤掉 因为它会在煮沸过程中积累起来，使糖浆看起来混浊，尝起来有沙砾感。

transcript.en: Once this has been done, the syrup is ready to be packaged so that it can be used for a whole variety of products.
transcript.zh: 一旦整个流程结束 糖浆就可以进行包装了 这样它就可以被用于各种各样的产品。

transcript.en: It takes 40 litres of sap to produce one litre of maple syrup so you can get an idea of how much is needed!
transcript.zh: 生产一升枫糖浆需要40升树液，所以你就可以想象到一共要需要多少！

transcript.en: So that's the basic process. In places like Quebec where ...
transcript.zh: 所以，以上就是枫糖浆的基本生产流程。在Quebec这样的地方...
